intro: Each martial art has its own clothes and its own name. Judo students wear a thick cotton jacket. School wrestlers wear a one-piece singlet. Sumo wrestlers wear a heavy cloth belt.
In this unit, you will learn what a belt color means. You will meet ranks with names like dan and kyu. You will also learn where names like karate, taekwondo and kung fu come from.
By the end, you can tell what a school mark shows. You can match an art to its land and its language. You can name a real date for a rank or a uniform.
bigQuestion: What do a uniform, a belt and a name tell us about where a martial art comes from?

The word karate is written a new way, meaning empty hand

Taekwondo becomes an Olympic medal sport in Sydney

write.prompt: Pick two arts from this unit, like judo and taekwondo. Tell where each one comes from. Tell what its name means or what its students wear. Use one real date from the unit, like 1883 for dan ranks or 2022 for Illinois girls wrestling.

title: Jacket and Belt

chapters.title: A School Mark
chapters.bigQuestion: What can a jacket, a belt or a singlet tell you about the room it comes from?

story.title: The Shelf by the Door
story.kicker: A jacket and a belt wait on a shelf, like books waiting for readers.
paragraphs: By the door of a judo club, there is a wooden shelf. On it sits a folded white jacket. It is thick cotton, heavy in your hands. A green belt is rolled up on top.
The shelf looks like a shelf in a library. Each jacket has a name tag. Each belt has a color. A new student reads the colors like the backs of books.
The belt is not magic. It is a mark, like a grade on a report card. It shows that a student has studied for a while. A teacher gives it out after watching and testing.
Down the hall, a wrestling team is getting ready. They do not wear jackets or belts at all. They wear a snug one-piece suit. Different rooms use different clothes.
story.think: What clothes or marks at your school show what class or team you are in?

lessons.title: The Judo Jacket
lessons.mainIdea: Judo students wear a thick cotton jacket and pants called a judogi.
reading: Kanō Jigorō opened a judo school in Tokyo in 1882. It was called the Kodokan. His students wore a thick cotton jacket, pants and a belt. This outfit is called a *judogi*.
In Japanese, gi means clothes. So judogi means judo clothes. Many people just say *gi*. For a long time, every judogi was white.
In the late 1990s, big judo contests began to use blue jackets too. One player wears white. The other wears blue. Now judges and fans can tell them apart.

words.d: the thick cotton jacket, pants and belt worn in judo
a Japanese word for clothes; a short name for a practice uniform

look.title: Two Jackets on a Mat
look.text: Look at a square mat under bright lights. One person stands in a white jacket. One person stands in a blue jacket. A judge in a suit stands between them. Big screens show their names.
look.prompt: How do the two colors help the judge and the people watching?

check.q: What does gi mean in Japanese?
check.why: Gi means clothes, so judogi means judo clothes.

check.q: Who opened the Kodokan judo school in 1882?
check.why: Kanō Jigorō opened the Kodokan in Tokyo in 1882.

check.q: Why do big judo contests use one white and one blue jacket?
choices: It helps people tell the two players apart.
check.why: Since the late 1990s, one white and one blue jacket help judges and fans tell the players apart.

lessons.title: From Street Clothes to White
lessons.mainIdea: Karate began in Okinawa without a uniform, and later took white clothes like judo's.
reading: *Karate* grew up on Okinawa. Okinawa is a chain of islands south of the main islands of Japan. It was once its own kingdom, called Ryukyu.
Early karate students in Okinawa trained in their everyday clothes. There were no special jackets and no colored belts.
In the 1920s, karate teachers from Okinawa taught in Tokyo. There, karate classes began to wear white suits much like the judogi. They also began to use belts and ranks like judo.

words.d: a martial art that grew up on Okinawa and later spread to Japan and the world
a chain of islands south of Japan's main islands; once the Ryukyu Kingdom

look.title: Then and Now
look.text: Picture two old photos side by side. In the first, a few men stand in a yard on Okinawa. They wear loose everyday clothes. In the second, a class in Tokyo stands in rows. Everyone wears a white suit with a belt.
look.prompt: What changed between the first photo and the second?

check.q: Where did karate grow up?
check.why: Karate grew up on Okinawa, once the Ryukyu Kingdom.

check.why: Early karate students trained in everyday clothes, with no special uniform.

check.why: In the 1920s, karate classes in Tokyo began wearing white suits much like the judogi.

lessons.title: Kanō's Ranks
lessons.mainIdea: In 1883, Kanō Jigorō began giving judo students ranks called dan.
reading: In 1883, Kanō Jigorō gave his first *dan* ranks. Dan means step or level. The first dan was for students who had studied hard for a long time.
Before dan came the *kyu* grades. Kyu grades are for students who are still learning the basics. Later, people with a dan rank wore a black belt. Newer students wore a white one.

words.d: a rank for advanced students; a black belt shows a dan rank
a grade for students who are still learning, before the dan ranks

look.title: Grades Like School
look.text: Look at a ladder with many steps. The low steps are marked kyu. The high steps are marked dan. A new student starts near the bottom. Each step up takes time and a test.
look.prompt: How is this ladder like moving up grades in school?

check.q: What does dan mean?
check.why: Dan means step or level. It is a rank for advanced students.

check.q: When did Kanō give his first dan ranks?
check.why: Kanō Jigorō gave the first dan ranks in 1883.

check.q: Who are kyu grades for?
check.why: Kyu grades come before dan. They are for students still learning.

lessons.title: Many Colors, Many Schools
lessons.mainIdea: A belt color is a mark a school gives, and each school can choose its own colors.
reading: At first, judo mostly used white and black belts. Later, teachers in Europe added more colors, like yellow, orange and green. A judo teacher in Paris named Mikonosuke Kawaishi is often named for this, in the 1930s.
Today, each art and each school can set its own colors. A green belt in one school may not mean the same in another. The *belt* is a school mark. It is not magic.
Taekwondo from Korea uses a black belt too. The Kukkiwon in Seoul, Korea, gives out taekwondo black belt papers called *certificates*.

words.d: a cloth band tied at the waist; its color shows a rank in that school
a paper that says a person earned a rank

look.title: Two Green Belts
look.text: Two students each hold up a green belt. One comes from a judo club in France. One comes from a karate club in Chicago. The belts look the same. The two clubs made their own color lists.
look.prompt: Do the two green belts have to mean the same thing? Why or why not?

check.q: What does a belt color show?
check.why: A belt color is a school mark. It shows a rank in that school.

check.q: Where did teachers add many belt colors to judo?
check.why: Judo teachers in Europe added colors like yellow, orange and green.

check.q: What does the Kukkiwon in Seoul give out?
check.why: The Kukkiwon in Seoul gives out certificates for taekwondo black belts.

lessons.title: The Wrestling Singlet
lessons.mainIdea: School wrestlers in Illinois wear a one-piece suit called a singlet.
reading: Wrestlers in school do not wear a gi or a belt. Most wear a *singlet*. A singlet is a snug suit made in one piece. It shows the team's colors.
School wrestlers also wear ear guards. Rules for high school wrestling say they must. The guards are straps with hard cups over each ear.
In Illinois, the IHSA runs school wrestling. Its first boys state champions were crowned in 1937. Its first girls state finals came in 2022.

words.d: a snug one-piece suit that wrestlers wear
the Illinois High School Association, which runs school sports in Illinois

check.why: A singlet is a snug one-piece suit that wrestlers wear.

check.why: The IHSA held its first girls wrestling state finals in 2022.

check.q: What do school wrestlers wear over their ears?
check.why: High school wrestling rules say wrestlers must wear ear guards.

lessons.title: Masks and Lights in Fencing
lessons.mainIdea: Fencers wear masks and white jackets, and a box with lights helps judges see each touch.
reading: Fencers wear a mask with a metal mesh front. They also wear a white jacket, gloves and long socks. The mask lets them see out while it keeps the face safe.
Long ago, judges watched with their eyes to see each touch. Then electric boxes came. A wire runs from the fencer to a *scoring box*. A light turns on when a touch lands.
Each of the three fencing swords got the lights at a different time. The épée got them at the 1936 Olympics. The foil got them in 1956. The sabre got them in 1988.

words.d: a helmet with a mesh front that fencers wear
an electric box whose lights show when a fencing touch lands

lessons.title: The Sumo Belt
lessons.mainIdea: Sumo wrestlers wear a thick belt called a mawashi, and a written list shows their ranks.
reading: Sumo wrestlers do not wear a jacket. They wear a thick cloth belt called a *mawashi*. Top wrestlers wear silk ones at the big contests. Others wear cotton.
Sumo ranks are not shown by belt colors. They are written on a list called the *banzuke*. A new banzuke comes out before each grand tournament. Japan holds six of them a year.
The highest rank is yokozuna. In a special ceremony, a yokozuna wears a thick white rope around his waist.

words.d: the thick cloth belt that sumo wrestlers wear
the written list of sumo ranks, made for each grand tournament
the highest rank in sumo

look.text: Look at a big sheet of paper covered with brush writing. The names at the top are written large. The names near the bottom are written very small. It is posted before a tournament in Tokyo.
look.prompt: Why might the top names be written bigger than the bottom names?

choices: the thick belt sumo wrestlers wear
check.why: The mawashi is the thick cloth belt of sumo.

check.q: How are sumo ranks shown?

check.why: Sumo ranks are written on the banzuke, a new one for each grand tournament.

check.q: What is the highest rank in sumo?
check.why: Yokozuna is the highest sumo rank. Dan and kyu are judo and karate ranks.

chapters.title: Many Names
chapters.bigQuestion: Why do martial arts from different places have different names?

story.title: Six Names on One Sign
story.kicker: A hallway sign lists six arts, and each name comes from a different place.
paragraphs: A community center has a long hallway. At the end hangs a sign with six names on it. Judo. Karate. Taekwondo. Kung fu. Muay Thai. Capoeira.
A girl named Rosa reads the sign slowly. She thinks they might be one family. But the names do not match at all. Each name comes from a different language.

Her grandpa points to each one. Judo is a Japanese word. Karate grew on Okinawa. Taekwondo is Korean. Kung fu is an English way to say a Chinese word. Muay Thai is from Thailand. Capoeira is from Brazil.
Rosa smiles. The sign is like a map. Each name tells her where an art began and what language its people speak. Six names point to six places.
story.think: Can you name a food or a game whose name comes from another language?

lessons.title: Judo Means the Gentle Way
lessons.mainIdea: Judo is a Japanese name that means the gentle way.
reading: Judo is a Japanese word with two parts. Ju means gentle or soft. *Do* means way or path. So judo means the gentle way.
Kanō Jigorō chose this name for his school in Tokyo. Many other arts from Japan end in do too. Kendo is the way of the sword. It uses bamboo swords and armor.
Sumo is also from Japan. It is much older than judo. Today the Japan Sumo Association runs the big sumo contests.

words.d: a Japanese and Korean word part meaning way or path
a Japanese art with bamboo swords and armor; its name means the way of the sword

look.title: Words That End the Same
look.text: Look at three names written on cards: judo, kendo, aikido. Each one ends with the same two letters. All three come from Japan. The end part, do, means way.
look.prompt: What part of each name is the same, and what does it mean?

check.q: What does judo mean?
check.why: Ju means gentle and do means way. So judo means the gentle way.

check.q: What does do mean in names like judo and kendo?
check.why: Do means way or path.

check.q: Which art uses bamboo swords and armor?
check.why: Kendo, the way of the sword, uses bamboo swords and armor.

lessons.title: Karate From Okinawa
lessons.mainIdea: Karate grew on Okinawa, and its name came to mean empty hand.
reading: The islands of Okinawa were once the Ryukyu Kingdom. The kingdom traded with China for hundreds of years. In 1879, Japan took over the islands.
Karate grew on Okinawa. At first, its name was written to mean China hand. In the 1930s, teachers began to write it a new way. The new way means *empty hand*.
Karate spread to Japan, and then the world. It was in the Olympics for the first time at the Tokyo Games, held in 2021.

words.d: the old kingdom on the Okinawa islands, before Japan took over in 1879
the meaning of the word karate as it has been written since the 1930s

look.title: One Name, Two Ways to Write It
look.text: Picture a teacher at a board. She writes the sound kara-te two ways. Under the first way she writes China hand. Under the second way she writes empty hand. The sound stays the same.
look.prompt: How can one name be spoken the same but mean two things?

check.q: What was Okinawa before 1879?
check.why: Okinawa was the Ryukyu Kingdom until Japan took over in 1879.

check.q: What does karate mean, as written since the 1930s?
check.why: Since the 1930s, karate has been written to mean empty hand.

check.q: When was karate first in the Olympics?
choices: at the Tokyo Games held in 2021
check.why: Karate was first in the Olympics at the Tokyo Games, held in 2021.

sections.title: Names From Korea, China and Thailand

lessons.title: Taekwondo From Korea
lessons.mainIdea: Taekwondo is a Korean art, and it is not the same as karate.
reading: *Taekwondo* comes from Korea. The name has three parts. Tae means foot. Kwon means fist. Do means way, just as in Japanese.
The name taekwondo was chosen in Korea in 1955. Karate and taekwondo are different arts. They come from different lands, with different languages and different rule books.
Taekwondo was shown at the 1988 Olympics in Seoul, Korea. It became a full Olympic sport with medals in 2000, in Sydney, Australia.

words.d: a martial art and sport from Korea; its name joins foot, fist and way

look.title: Two Cards, Two Countries
look.text: Look at two cards on a table. One says karate, Okinawa, Japanese words. The other says taekwondo, Korea, Korean words. Both have a picture of a white uniform and a black belt.
look.prompt: The uniforms look alike. What makes the two arts different?

check.q: Where does taekwondo come from?
check.why: Taekwondo is a Korean art. Karate grew on Okinawa.

check.q: When did taekwondo become a full Olympic sport with medals?
check.why: It was shown in 1988 and became a medal sport in 2000, in Sydney.

check.q: Are karate and taekwondo the same art?
choices: Yes, they are two names for one art.
No, they come from different lands and languages.
check.why: Karate grew on Okinawa and taekwondo in Korea. They are different arts.

lessons.title: Kung Fu Is a Wide Word
lessons.mainIdea: Kung fu is a wide English word for many different Chinese martial arts.
reading: *Kung fu* is an English way to say a Chinese word. In Chinese, the word can mean any skill that takes hard work and time. A great cook can have kung fu too.
China is a huge country with many regions. It has hundreds of martial arts styles, not one. Tai chi and wing chun are two of them. In China, many people call these arts *wushu*.
The words kung fu became well known in English in the 1970s. Films and TV shows spread them.

words.d: an English word for many Chinese martial arts; in Chinese it means skill from hard work
a Chinese word for martial arts

look.title: A Big Umbrella
look.text: Picture a big umbrella with the words kung fu on it. Under it stand many small signs. One says tai chi. One says wing chun. Many more signs fill the space. Each sign is its own style.
look.prompt: Why is kung fu called a wide word?

check.q: What can kung fu mean in Chinese?
choices: a skill from hard work and time
check.why: In Chinese, the word means a skill that takes hard work and time.

check.q: How many martial arts styles does China have?
check.why: China has hundreds of styles, like tai chi and wing chun.

check.q: What do many people in China call martial arts?
check.why: Wushu is a Chinese word for martial arts.

lessons.title: Muay Thai From Thailand
lessons.mainIdea: Muay Thai is the national sport of Thailand, and muay means boxing.
reading: Muay Thai comes from Thailand. In the Thai language, *muay* means boxing. So Muay Thai means Thai boxing.
Muay Thai is called the national sport of Thailand. Big stadiums in Bangkok hold matches many nights of the week. Lumpinee and Rajadamnern are two famous ones.
Before a match, many fighters honor their teachers with a slow ceremony. It is called the *wai khru*. Wai means to show respect. Khru means teacher.

words.d: the Thai word for boxing
a ceremony before a Muay Thai match that honors teachers

look.title: A Thank-You Before the Match
look.text: Look at a ring under bright lights in Bangkok. Music plays. A fighter moves slowly around the ring, alone. He is thanking his teachers before the match. The crowd waits quietly.
look.prompt: Why might someone thank a teacher before a big day?

check.q: What does muay mean in Thai?
check.why: Muay is the Thai word for boxing.

check.q: What is the wai khru?
check.why: The wai khru is a ceremony that honors teachers before a match.

check.q: In which city are the Lumpinee and Rajadamnern stadiums?
check.why: Lumpinee and Rajadamnern are famous Muay Thai stadiums in Bangkok.

sections.title: Names From Islands, Brazil and Europe

lessons.title: Arnis and Silat
lessons.mainIdea: Arnis comes from the Philippines, and pencak silat comes from Indonesia and nearby lands.
reading: *Arnis* comes from the Philippines. It is also called eskrima or kali. It is known for its sticks. In 2009, a Philippine law named arnis the country's national martial art and sport.
*Pencak silat* comes from Indonesia and nearby lands, like Malaysia. There are many styles on many islands. In 2019, UNESCO honored pencak silat as part of the world's heritage.

words.d: a martial art from the Philippines, also called eskrima or kali
martial arts from Indonesia and nearby lands, with many styles

look.text: Look at a poster from the Philippines. At the top it says arnis. Under that it says eskrima. Under that it says kali. A pair of rattan sticks is drawn below the words.
look.prompt: Why might one art have three different names?

check.why: Arnis, also called eskrima or kali, comes from the Philippines.

lessons.title: Old Names From Europe
lessons.mainIdea: Fencing, boxing and wrestling from Europe were in the Olympics long before judo or taekwondo.
reading: Europe gave its own names to its arts. Many fencing words are French. Boxing rules grew in England. Capoeira, from Brazil, has a Portuguese name.
*Greco-Roman wrestling* has a name that sounds very old. But the style took shape in France in the 1800s. People named it to honor old Greece and Rome.
Fencing and wrestling were in the first modern Olympics in 1896. Boxing joined in 1904. Judo came in 1964, and taekwondo in 2000.

words.d: a style of wrestling that took shape in France in the 1800s, named for old Greece and Rome
world games held every four years; the modern Olympics began in 1896
